frequ. (in Talm. Y.) dropped in the beginning of words, e.g. בָּא = אַבָּא; מַר = אֲמַר.
affixed to the end of Chald. nouns, corresponding to prefixed ה in Hebrew (status emphaticus), e.g. אַבָּא = הָאָב.

definicoes_originais: as numeral letter, one, as אות א' = אות אחת one letter.
notas_originais: Sabb. 104 a; a. fr. [Editions and Mss. vary, according to space, between the full numeral and the numeral letter, א' for אחד, אחת; ב' for שנים, שתים, שתי &c.]
&c. a prefix,
for the formation of nouns in Kal, Peel, Afel (Hifil) &c., e.g. אִסְפְּקָא, אִיסְ', אַפְטָרָה, אַפְטַרְתָּא &c.;
demonstrative, e.g. אִיהוּ = h. הַהוּא; אִנָּא, אִינָא &c.
euphonic (prosthetic) אִדְמָא = דְּמָא; אִית = h. יֵשׁ &c., esp. before foreign words beginning with two consonants, e.g. אִסְטְרָטֵיגוֹס, אִיסְ' = סְטַרְטֵיגֹוס &c.

definicoes_originais: (Assyr. A-bu, Schr. K. A. T., p. 247) Ab, the fifth month of the Jewish calendar (of thirty days) beginning between the eighth of July and the seventh of August, and ending between the sixth of August and the fifth of September.

definicoes_originais: , const. אֲבִי, אַב [embracer], father, ancestor, progenitor; teacher; chief, leader; author, originator.
fathers, ancestors, patriarchs &c. Ber. 26 b prayers א' תקנום have been instituted by the Patriarchs; a. fr.—אבות בתי דינין, v. supra. Ḥag. II, 2.
Aboth, the first section of the Prayer of Benedictions (v. תְּפִלָּה), so called because it alludes to the Patriarchs.

Aboth, name of a treatise of the Mishnah, containing sayings of Talmudic authorities and belonging to the fourth section, נזיקין, of the Mishnah collection (משניות); also styled פִּרְקֵי א' a. מְסֶכֶת א'.
notas_originais: Ex. R. s. 46 end המגדל אב the educator is the real father. Lev. R. s. 1 אבי החכמה וכ', the father of all wisdom, … the father of prophets. Y. Ned. V, 39 b; a. fr.—אַב בית דין (abbr. אב"ד) president of the Court (Great Sanhedrin), next in dignity to the Nassi. Taan. II, 1; a. fr.—Metaph. origin, cause. Num. R. s. 10 (play on אֲבוֹי, Prov. XXIII, 29) א' אוי the cause of woe (sin).—אב מלאכה (for which also עיקר) one of the chief labors forbidden on the Sabbath, opp. תולדה a labor the prohibition of which is based on the ground of its being a species of the former, or derived from the former. Sabb. VII, 1 sq.; a. fr.—[Y. Sabb. II, 5 a, אב שלה, sub. מלאכה.]—אב הטומאה one of the original or direct causes of levitical uncleanness, opp. ולד (child) secondary cause. Toh. I, 5; a. fr.—א' הנזק v. Pl.—בנין א' creation of a class, i.e. a conclusion, by analogy, from a case explicitly stated in the bibl. law on all similar cases not specified in detail. Sifra introd.—Ib. K’doshim, end, ch. 11 (ref. to Lev. XX, 27) זה ב' א' לכל דמיהם בם this forms the rule for all cases in which the Bible uses the word d’mēhem bam (that the penalty is stoning to death); a. fr.; v. also בֵּית אב.— Pl. אָבוֹת־, const. אֲבוֹת,

—בת א' a woman of noble descent. Num. R. s. 1; a. e.—Metaph. principal, chief א' מלאכות, v. supra. א' הטומא' Kel. I, 1; v. supra.—א' נזיקין (sing. אב הנזק) the chief actionable injuries or damages, from which the subordinate are deduced (תולדות). B. Kam. I, 1; a. e.
R. Hash. IV, 5; a. fr.
A similar collection of a later date is contained in Talmud Babli editions, named א' דרבי נתן Aboth d’Rabbi Nathan. [Y. Yoma VIII, 44 d top אב בית נפש v. אֲבֵידָה.]

stall, stable.
notas_originais: Ned. IV, 4.—Sabb. 140 b אי' של כלי (Rashi אב') a real manger, opp. אי' של קרקע a piece of ground fenced in and used as manger.
Y. Shebu. VII, 37 d top; VIII, beg. 38 b. [Y. Ter. I, 40 b אבוס read אִכּוּם or אָכִים.]— Pl. אֵבוּסִים. Y. Snh. 63 b אֵבוּסֵיהֶן their stables. V. אֵיפוּס.

definicoes_originais: Abuka.
notas_originais: Yalk. Lam. 1001, v. אֲבִיקָה.

definicoes_originais: (אבק, cmp. אבך, חבק; v. Sachs Beitr. I, p. 62; Naḥm. to Gen. XXXII, 25) [ bundle of twigs], torch (with, or without של אור).
notas_originais: Sot. 21 a נזדמנה לו א' של אור a burning torch happened to come in his possession. Ber. 43 b א' כשנים walking by torchlight is equal to two walking together (as regards protection from night-spirits).— Pl. אֲבוּקוֹת. Tosef. Succ. IV, 2 were dancing before them בא' with torches. Ib. 4 בשמונה א' של אור; Succ. 53 a ח' א' של אור; Y. ib. V, 55 c top א' של זהב (corr. acc. or read זֶפֶת?); Mish. ib. V, 4.

definicoes_originais: (Ar.) m. (= אִמְבּוּרְקְלוֹן q. v.; a Babyl.
notas_originais: corrupt. of an imported Palestinean phrase) bed-cover, ticking (involucrum). Pl. אַבּוּרְגְּנֵי, אַבְּרוּ'. Erub. 62 a בריאה במוהרקי וא' a lease of a court yard is called sound (legal and not merely a legal fiction), if connected with the privilege of placing in the yard chairs and seats, [Rashi, cmp. Mishnah;—מוהרקי, obviously a corruption for גוהרקי or גלופקרי, cmp. גמורקין.—Other explanations of our w., suggested by מוהרקי, v. s. v. מוה'.]
, v. אַכְוַר'

definicoes_originais: (בזק) breaking, crumbling, corrosion, whence
a foot-disease in animals believed to arise from vermin in consequence of a stroke of lightning;
moth-eaten condition of garments.
notas_originais: B. Mets. 78 b (expl. הבריקה Mish.) אבזקת (Rashi אבזקא, Ms. M. אבוק, corr. ז for ו; cmp. Y. ib. VI, 11 a top. s. v. בָּזָק) atrophy or paralysis of the feet. Ib. א' במילת' וכ' the moths are in the royal wardrobe.

definicoes_originais: (Arab. bazr, abzār, v. בזר, פזר) anything used for seasoning, spices &c.—Fig.
notas_originais: requisites, appurtenances. Snh. 74 b אינהו וכל אבזרייהו they (the commands) and all appertaining thereto. Men. 73 b עולה וכל אֲבִיזְרָהָא Ar. a. Rashi to Snh. l. c. (ed. חבירתא corr. acc.) the burnt-offering and &c.

definicoes_originais: (בט; cmp. בוט, בוץ, בטט a. deriv.) belly, whence leather wine-bag.
notas_originais: Ab. Zar. 34 b א' דטייעי (Ar. אכטא) the travellers’ wine-bag. [Y. Yeb. IV, 5 d, v. אֶפְטָא.] [אבטאות, v. אַבְּטִי.]

definicoes_originais: (prob. Πτολεμαῖος, or Εὐπτόλεμος = Εὐπόλεμος) Abtolmos.
notas_originais: Erub. III, 4 (35 a) ed. (Ms. M. אבטולס). Ib. 36 a; Y. ib. 21 a bot. אבטילס (v. Rabb. D. S. Erub. l. c., notes). Ex. R. s. 21 (אבטלוס) אבטוליס.—M. Kat. 18 a אֲבִיטוּל (prob. abbrev. of our w.), surnamed ספראה (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.), an Amora.

definicoes_originais: (αὐτόματος) self-moving, self-growing, spontaneous.
notas_originais: Midr. Till. to Ps. I, 5 האומרים א' הוא העולם Mus. (ed. טומטום, corr. acc.) who say the universe is a self-moving power (has no creator). [Better: אַבְטוֹמְטוֹן (αὐτόματον, S.) chance.]

notas_originais: Y. Meg. I, 70 a bot. שני א' (read שתי). Y. B. Bath. III, 14 a top אבטנ'; Bekh. 55 a שני אבטילאות (corr. acc., Ar. אבטלאות, אבטליות). [Cmp. corruptions of אַגְרוֹנִימוֹס.]
